summary: Implemented line-oriented regex matching over complete physical records. Regex requests now use the selected cached backend, reader-block boundaries cannot change record anchors or greedy selection, zero-width matches progress through each record, whole-word boundaries use the declared Unicode policy, and record growth is bounded.

review.reviewer: separate grill-code review pass (no independent subagent was available)

startingState.worktree: Tracked files were clean at scope start; ignored campaign state recorded W07-S02 as in_progress.
startingState.aheadNote: The ahead count includes the reachable completed Search scope commits through W07-S01 and other pre-existing branch commits; no upstream changes were present.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning Search source, tests and Search documentation were changed. The ignored local campaign state was not staged. No sibling repository, SQL/XML surface, release, publication or installation was modified.
implementation.requestMode: An internal Regex pattern mode constructs and validates a request before source enumeration; existing public two-argument Search constructors remain literal.

recordScanner.crlfPolicy: CR immediately before LF is treated as the terminator for regex input; line rows retain CRLF text.
recordScanner.blockBoundaryPolicy: Accumulate one complete physical record across reader blocks; never use a guessed fixed overlap.
recordScanner.emptyInput: An empty file has no physical records; an empty record between LF delimiters is evaluated.
recordScanner.zeroWidthProgress: Relies on Regex.Matches leftmost-first enumeration, which advances after a zero-width result; mapped zero-width spans carry byte length zero when the boundary is provable.
recordScanner.wholeWordPolicy: Accepted regex matches are filtered with SearchWordPolicy, including supplementary scalars and combining marks.

implementation.sinkIntegration: Occurrence rows receive the actual regex match text when projected; line sinks receive one completed physical line after all accepted matches; files and counts retain their existing row units and early/completed-scan behavior.

newScenarios: Regex rows apply record anchors and source-order alternatives
Greedy alternatives remain within one physical record and cannot cross LF
Zero-width matches progress once per record and carry zero byte length
Regex results are invariant to irregular reader-block boundaries
Regex lines emit one row per matching physical record with occurrence counts
Regex whole-word filtering uses Unicode scalar boundaries
Records beyond 1,048,576 UTF-16 characters fail with a typed resource diagnostic
UTF-8 regex spans retain original-byte coordinates
An empty file produces no regex rows
requiredCoverage: Anchors and greedy alternatives are evaluated against complete physical records.
Newline delimiters isolate records and are not matched as record content.
Zero-width results progress without an infinite loop.
Giant records are rejected before regex execution and empty input terminates cleanly.

The separate ownership review approved complete-record accumulation, coordinate mapping, zero-width progression, record/resource bounds and scope boundaries; exact commands, tool versions, source/artifact hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are recorded and verified during post-commit finalization.
Focused integration tests cover the documented record-anchor, source-order, greedy, newline-isolation, zero-width, whole-word, coordinate, empty-input and giant-record cases.
The regex request mode is internal and no public SQL/XML metadata, query example or advertised contract was changed; capture-row exposure remains W07-S03.

The scanner retains only one bounded record and aligned coordinate list, checks cancellation while reading and matching, does not retain reader-block buffers, and preserves the backend's bounded immutable regex cache and timeout.

knownLimitations: This scope implements complete-record regex execution without capture-row exposure; captures remain W07-S03.
A regex record is intentionally bounded to 1,048,576 UTF-16 characters; longer records fail rather than being split with an unsound overlap.
The regex request mode is an internal foundation and does not yet add a public SQL/XML regex constructor or many-pattern transport.
The repository-wide suite retains 31 existing expected skips and 3 platform-conditional symlink skips; no package was published, pushed, released or installed.
